sentences.text: 2. Heard learned counsel for the appellants and learned counsel for the State.
3. It appears that notice has validly been served but nobody has appeared on behalf of the victim.

4. The appeal has been preferred against the impugned order dated 24.02.2024 in A.B.P. No.53 of 2024 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-I, Sahibganj in connection with Sahibganj SC/ST P.S. Case No.13 of 2019 corresponding to G.R. Case No.454 of 2019, registered for the offence under Sections 341, 323, 354(B), 376, 406, 420, 506 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code and under Section 3(1)(e)(S) of the SC/ST (PoA) Act.

The case is presently pending in the court of the learned Special Judge (SC/ST Court), Sahibganj.
5.
It appears that it is the third attempt for grant of anticipatory bail.

Earlier the first anticipatory bail application being Cr. Appeal (S.J.) No.1040 of 2019 was dismissed as withdrawn on 14.02.2022 and another one being Cr. Appeal (S.J.) No.14 of 2024 was also dismissed as withdrawn on 02.02.2024.
6. It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the appellants that during the investigation the police has found that most of the allegations are false.
The appellants undertake to participate in the trial.
On the above basis, the prayer for anticipatory bail has been made.
7. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail.
8. It is settled law that anticipatory bail is not maintainable under the SC/ST (PoA) Act.

Otherwise,
the nature of allegations also suggests that there is serious allegation against these appellants.
9. Considering the nature of allegation and mandate of the SC/ST (PoA) Act, I am not inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the appellants.
Accordingly, the present criminal appeal stands rejected.

(Rajesh Kumar, J.) Amar/-
